A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. v4 retains Appendices A–I, expands Appendix B, and adds Appendix J.

before.justification: v3 reports original policy-training experiments, accuracy–efficiency evaluations on mathematical and coding tasks, transfer experiments, and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, test-time probability-scaling experiments, non-greedy decoding evaluations, and policy-input ablations.

M1.justification: v4 adds inference-time scaling of Bernoulli probabilities to min(1, beta times s), allowing one trained policy to vary its speed (Section 4.1). It also adapts confidence inputs for non-greedy decoding. The policy architecture, GRPO training, rewards, DPLS alternative, and expert steering remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, MATH/MATH-500, HumanEval, MBPP, and KodCode-RL-10K, retaining the same mathematical and coding coverage. The new decoding procedures, input ablations, and GSM8K subset concern experimental settings within that coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds Margin sampling from Kim et al. and EB Sampler from Ben-Hamu et al. to the LLaDA comparisons on both mathematical datasets and both block lengths (Figure 11; Tables 2–5). These methods were cited but not evaluated in v3. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: v4 substantially extends evaluation beyond the retained greedy protocols: Figure 19 uses temperature 0.8, candidate counts up to 32, pass@k, majority voting, and outcome-reward-model selection, with 300 GSM8K test problems. It also adds probability-scaling sweeps and controlled test-time input interventions. Original training and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether probability scaling improves controllability, whether stochastic policies support better multiple-sample decoding, and whether time and mask inputs are necessary (Figures 6, 19, and 20). These substantially extend the retained reward, likelihood, confidence-input, temperature, seed-sensitivity, and trajectory analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same training-seed selection, three test-time seeds, and existing uncertainty bands and seed-spread displays. Appendix J tabulates uncertainty for already plotted results; it does not specify additional runs, a new estimator, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Existing result plots are unchanged, but v4 adds substantial results for probability scaling, additional baselines, non-greedy decoding, and input ablations. Figure 19 reports new pass@32 advantages of 1.46 percentage points on GSM8K and 3.58 on MATH-500. Their simple mean is 2.52 points, differing from Section 4.3's stated 2.56. Appendix J mainly tabulates plotted results.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 adds a definition of confidence for non-greedy decoding using the probability of the sampled token, extending v3's maximum-probability definition. The MDP formulation, objectives, and Appendix E–G derivations remain unchanged; sequence-length notation edits do not change their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the same central claims: lightweight RL policies on frozen dLLMs match heuristic performance under semi-AR generation and outperform heuristics under full diffusion. The added conclusion sentence summarizes transfer and design insights already claimed in v3.

C2.justification: v4 revises the controllability limitation in light of successful test-time scaling and interprets non-greedy results as improved exploration and resistance to diversity collapse. It adds interpretations of input dependence, although Section 4.4's blanket accuracy-drop statement overlooks Figure 20's exception for removing time alone on GSM8K.

D1.justification: v4 adds a first-page code-repository link and specifies configurations for the new decoding and input-ablation experiments. The existing algorithm, A100 hardware disclosure, architecture diagram, and Table 1 training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New citations support probability scaling, sampling-diversity discussion, multimodal extensions, and outcome reward modeling, including Chen, Ni, Olausson, Bethune, and Liu et al. The principal positioning against heuristic sampling, RL post-training, and distillation remains stable. Kim's changed citation suffix and Zhan's updated title refer to retained works.

P1.justification: v4 adds localized experimental paragraphs and appendix entries, rewrites the limitations paragraph, corrects Section 5 cross-references, and standardizes some terminology and headings. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v4 redraws the central sampling schematic in Figure 2 and substantially expands the displays through Figures 6, 11, 19, and 20 and Appendix J's four numerical tables. Existing figures are largely retained and renumbered. The tables redisplay plotted values rather than constitute four new experiments.

improvement.justification: v4 partly addresses v3's acknowledged controllability limitation with a tested inference-time option and strengthens empirical support through additional comparators and analyses. Exact tables and code-access information make the work easier to check. These are useful, bounded gains: the control evidence remains confined to the tested LLaDA mathematical setting, and small inconsistencies between the prose and Figures 19–20 reduce precision.
